brief: Aggregate equity positioning stayed resilient at modestly overweight levels (60th percentile) despite rising rates volatility, but a divergence sits beneath it: large caps are overweight (85th percentile) while small caps have slipped to modestly underweight (43rd percentile), and systematic strategies hold elevated exposure (92nd percentile) even as discretionary investors drifted below neutral (27th-29th percentile), a pattern the note ties to rising rates vol specifically, which it argues is the key driver for equities, not the level of rates. Sector positioning is narrow: MCG & Tech is the only clear overweight while cyclicals and defensives sit at or below neutral. The rotation into Tech extended another 2pp this week and is nearing levels from which it has reversed several times before. CTAs and risk-parity funds remain elevated across most asset classes, long dollar and commodities, short gold. Weekly flows: equity funds took in $15.8bn (DM-led, US still extending outflows), bond funds $18.8bn (led by government bonds and munis), while money-market funds saw $118.0bn of outflows, led by the US and a record outflow in Europe.
